name: GABA (gamma-aminobutyric acid) supplements
short: Raised liver enzyme (AST) in 9 of 35 men on a GABA drug formulation for 6 months (2 withdrew); dizziness, sore throat in a week-long study. Review: blood pressure drop; no pregnancy data.
text: Liver enzyme rises: in a 6-month randomised trial of a controlled-release GABA formulation taken by mouth in 35 men with long-standing type 1 diabetes (one arm also took alprazolam for 3 months), the aspartate aminotransferase (AST) liver enzyme rose in nine men, leading two to withdraw; most rises were transient and did not differ by dose, and the authors report that side effects were commonly observed. In an open-label study in 12 healthy volunteers, the 7-day period of repeated GABA by mouth was followed by more minor adverse events than the placebo or single-dose periods, mainly transient dizziness and sore throat, with no serious adverse events. In a 4-week randomised trial of GABA from fermented rice germ in 40 people with insomnia (30 given GABA, 10 placebo), adverse events occurred in four people (10%); the abstract does not say in which groups, and the authors report no severe adverse events. In a one-year randomised trial in 97 children with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes (41 given oral GABA, 25 GABA with GAD-alum, 31 placebo), the authors state that the safety and tolerability of GABA were confirmed, without giving event figures. A 2021 safety review by the United States Pharmacopeia, covering GABA as a dietary supplement or as a natural constituent of fermented milk or soy, found no serious adverse events at intakes up to 18 g a day for 4 days or 120 mg a day for 12 weeks, and no case reports or spontaneous adverse event reports; some studies showed a transient, moderate drop in blood pressure (less than 10%). Pregnancy: the review found no studies in pregnancy or breastfeeding and advises caution for pregnant and breastfeeding women, because GABA can affect neurotransmitters and hormones (it raises growth hormone and prolactin levels). In the combination supplement of fish oil, lactoferrin, zinc, vitamin C, lutein, vitamin E, GABA and Enterococcus faecium tested for dry eye (8 weeks, 40 volunteers randomised), no adverse events occurred; this result belongs to the combination. Interactions: the review says that, because GABA has lowered blood pressure in some studies, it is conceivable that taking it with blood pressure medicines could increase the risk of low blood pressure; this is a theoretical risk, not an observed interaction.
